The commentary on His words, ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾, and here are some issues:

The first issue: Know that it is God's custom in the Qur'an that whenever He mentions the angels in the context of awe and warning, He singles out the Spirit (al-Ruh) for mention after them, as in this verse, and as in His words, ﴿The Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows﴾ [al-Naba: 38]. This indicates that the Spirit is greater in rank than the angels. Here there is a subtle point: when He mentioned the ascent, He mentioned the angels first and the Spirit second, as in this verse, and when He mentioned standing, He mentioned the Spirit first and the angels second, as in His words, ﴿The Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows﴾. This indicates that the Spirit is first in the order of descent and last in the order of ascent. For this reason some of the mystics (al-mukashifun) said: The Spirit is a great light, the nearest of lights to the majesty of God, and from it branch out the spirits of all the other angels and of humans at the lowest stations of the degrees of spirits. Between the two extremes lie the ascending levels of the angelic spirits and the stages of the holy lights, and none knows their quantity except God. As for the apparent view of the theologians (al-mutakallimun) that the Spirit is Gabriel (peace be upon him), we have established this question in the commentary on His words, ﴿The Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows﴾.

The second issue: Those who argue that God is in a place, either in the Throne or above it, have used this verse in two ways.

The first: The verse describes God as ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, and He is so described only if He is in the direction of above.

The second: His words, ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴾, show that the ascent and rising of the angels is toward Him, and this requires that He be in the direction of above.

The answer: Since the proofs have established that God cannot be in a place or a direction, it follows that interpretation (ta'wil) is necessary. As for describing God as ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, we have mentioned the possible meanings of it. As for the particle ﴿ilayhi﴾ (to Him) in His words, ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴾, it does not mean a place; rather it means that affairs end at His will, as in His words, ﴿And to Him all affairs are returned﴾ [Hud: 123]. It means arriving at the place of honor and dignity, as in His words, ﴿I am going to my Lord﴾ [al-Saffat: 99]. This points to the fact that the abode of reward is the highest and loftiest of places.

The third issue: Most scholars hold that His words, ﴿in a Day﴾, are connected to ﴿ta'ruju﴾ (ascend), meaning that the ascent takes place in a day like this. Muqatil said: Rather, this is connected to His words, ﴿with a punishment that will befall﴾. According to this view, there is a transposition in the verse, and the meaning is: A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall, in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years. According to the first interpretation, that Day is either in the Hereafter or in this world. If it is in the Hereafter, that length is either actual or estimated. These are the possibilities the verse carries, and we will mention their details.

The first view: The meaning of the verse is that this ascent takes place in one of the days of the Hereafter, whose length is fifty thousand years, and this is the Day of Resurrection. This is the view of al-Hasan, who said: It does not mean that its measure is only this, for if it were so, it would have an end, and Paradise and Hell would perish at that end, and this is impossible. Rather, what is meant is that their standing for reckoning, until people are judged, is fifty thousand years of the years of this world. After that, the people of Hell will settle in the depths of the fires; we seek refuge in God from them. Know that this length applies only to the unbeliever, but not to the believer, and the evidence for this is the verse and the report. As for the verse, it is His words, ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better resting place and a finer place of repose﴾ [al-Furqan: 24]. They agree that that place of repose and resting is Paradise. As for the report, it is what was related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that he said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "What is the length of this Day?" He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, it will be lightened for the believer until it is lighter for him than a prescribed prayer which he prays in the world." Some people have said: Even if that standing is long, it will be a cause of increased joy and comfort for the people of Paradise, and a cause of increased sorrow and distress for the people of Hell. The answer to this: The Hereafter is the abode of recompense, so the rewards of those who are rewarded must be hastened to them, and the abode of reward is Paradise, not the standing place. Therefore, the length of the standing must be specified for the unbelievers.

The second view: This period is an actual event in the Hereafter, but by way of estimation, not by way of certainty. The meaning is that if the most intelligent and sharpest of creatures were occupied with that judgment and decision, it would last fifty thousand years. Then God would complete that judgment and decision in the measure of half a day of the days of this world. Also, the angels ascend to places where, if one of the people of this world wished to ascend to them, he would spend fifty thousand years in that ascent, but they ascend to them in a short while. This is the view of Wahb and a group of the exegetes.

The third view, which is the view of Abu Muslim: This Day is the day of the whole world, from the time God created until the end of annihilation. God thus made clear that in the day of this world there must be the ascent and descent of the angels, and this day is measured as fifty thousand years. It does not follow from this that the time of the Resurrection becomes known, because we do not know how much has passed and how much remains.

The fourth view: The verse is to be read as: A questioner asked about a punishment from God that will befall, in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years. It is possible that what is meant is the lengthening of that Day because of its severity upon the unbelievers. It is also possible that what is meant is the measuring of its duration. According to this, the intention is not that the punishment is measured by this amount, but rather to draw attention to the length of the duration of the punishment. It is also possible that the punishment which that questioner asked for will be fixed at this duration, and then God will transfer it to another kind of punishment after that.

The meaning of *yubassaruna-hum* is that they are made to recognize them, i.e., each close friend is made to recognize the other, until he knows him. **Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 70, verses 17–19:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It calls out to those who turned their backs and withdrew﴾ ﴿and gathered [wealth] and hoarded it﴾. On this there are two issues.

**The first issue:** The scholars differ over how Laza (Hellfire) can call out to the disbelievers, and they have mentioned several explanations.

The first is that it calls them with the tongue of its state (*lisan al-hal*), as it is said: "Ask the earth: who split your rivers and planted your trees? If it does not answer you with a cry, it answers you with a lesson." Here, since each of the disbelievers returns to a corner of Jahannam, it is as if those places call them and summon them.

The second is that Allah Almighty creates speech in the substance of the Fire, so that it says plainly: "Come to me, O disbeliever! Come to me, O hypocrite!" and then it snatches them up as a bird snatches grain.

The third is that what is meant is that the guardians of the Fire (*zabaniyah*) are the ones who call, and that call is attributed to the Fire by omitting the word that is governed (*bi-hadhf al-mudaf*).

The fourth is that *tad'u* means "destroys," from the Arabs' saying *da'aka Allah*, meaning "Allah destroy you." And His saying ﴿who turned his back and withdrew﴾ means: who turned his back on obedience and withdrew from faith. ﴿And gathered﴾ means [wealth], ﴿and hoarded it﴾ means: he placed it in a container and stored it, and did not pay the zakah and the obligatory rights due from it. So His saying ﴿turned his back and withdrew﴾ refers to turning away from knowing Allah and obeying Him, and His saying ﴿gathered and hoarded﴾ refers to love of this world: "gathered" refers to greed, and "hoarded" refers to hope [for long life]. And there is no doubt that the sum of the afflictions of religion is nothing but these.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, man was created anxious﴾ (*halu'an*). On this there are several issues.

**The first issue:** Some have said that what is meant by "man" here is the disbeliever. Others have said rather that it is general, as evidenced by His exception from it: ﴿except those who pray﴾.

**[Page 114]**

**The second issue:** It is said: *hali'a al-rajul yahla'u halaʿan wa halaʾan fa-huwa hali'un wa halu'un*, and it means extreme greed and little patience. It is said: "He went hungry and became anxious (*fa-halaʿa*)." Al-Farra' said: *al-halu'* is one who is greatly distressed (*al-dajur*). Al-Mubarrad said: *al-halaʿ* is impatience (*al-dajar*). It is said: "We seek refuge in Allah from anxiety (*halaʿ*) when facing rivals." It is related from Ahmad ibn Yahya, who said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Tahir said to me: "What is *halaʿ*?" I said: "Allah has already explained it, and there is no clearer explanation than His explanation: it is the one who, when evil befalls him, shows intense distress, and when good reaches him, he becomes miserly and withholds it from people."

**The third issue:** The Qadi said: His saying ﴿Indeed, man was created anxious﴾ is similar to His saying ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ [al-Anbiya: 37]. What is not meant is that he is created upon this attribute. The evidence for this is that Allah Almighty censured him for it, and Allah does not censure what is His own act. Also, He Almighty excepted the believers who struggled against their own selves to abandon this blameworthy trait; and if this trait were a necessary disposition created by the creation of Allah Almighty, they would not have been able to abandon it.

Know that *halaʿ* is a term applied to two things:

One of them is the inner state (*al-halah al-nafsaniyyah*) which causes a person to proceed to display distress and supplication.

The second is those outward acts of speech and action which indicate that inner state. As for that inner state, there is no doubt that it arises by the creation of Allah Almighty, because one whose soul was created in that state cannot remove that state from his soul; and one who was created brave and valiant cannot remove that state from his soul. Rather, the outward acts of speech and action he can abandon or undertake, so these are voluntary matters. As for the inner state which is in reality *halaʿ*, it is created by way of compulsion.
